text: We consider first the interior regularity of weak solutions to the boundary-value problem, and establish that a weak solution belongs to H^2 on any compactly contained subdomain, with a quantitative estimate.

THEOREM 1 (Interior H^2-regularity). Assume the coefficients a^{ij} are C^1 and f is in L^2. Suppose u in H_0^1(U) is a weak solution of the elliptic equation. Then u belongs to H_loc^2(U), and for each V compactly contained in U we have the estimate
the constant C depending only on V, U and the coefficients of the operator.
We turn next to regularity up to the boundary, which requires additional smoothness assumptions on the domain.
